chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is in prayer and sees a snake beside him, is it permissible for him to reach out and kill it? He said: 'If there is one step between him and it, let him step and kill it; otherwise, no.'

key_terms.يَتَنَاَلَهَا: To reach out/take hold of it

ai.seo_question: Can I kill a snake during prayer if it is close to me?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical criterion for breaking prayer (*khuruj min al-salah*) based on the proximity of a distracting danger, specifically a snake. The ruling balances the preservation of the prayer's integrity with the need to remove a potential threat, allowing movement only if the snake is within one step, thereby preventing unnecessary disruption of the worship.
